Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which award did Vicente Cárcel Orti receive?
Document 1: As the sun set over the sprawling city of Leipzig, Vicente Cárcel Orti, a Spanish historian and priest, stood nervously in the grand hall of the East German Ministry of Culture. He adjusted his clerical collar, a habit he'd developed over the years, and smoothed out the wrinkles on his worn tweed jacket. The air was thick with the scent of old books and stale cigarette smoke, a familiar aroma that transported him back to the dusty archives of Madrid's Biblioteca Nacional. Before him, a sea of stern-faced officials and intellectuals milled about, their eyes fixed on the podium where the Minister of Culture, a stout man with a bushy mustache, was about to announce the winner of the prestigious National Prize of East Germany. Vicente's heart raced as he thought about the months of research, the countless hours pouring over documents and conducting interviews, all leading up to this moment. As the Minister began to speak, Vicente's mind wandered back to his humble beginnings in the small town of Valencia, where his love for history was first kindled by his abuela's stories of the Spanish Civil War. He recalled the countless nights spent poring over dusty tomes in the local library, devouring the works of Marx and Engels, and later, the writings of East German historians who had inspired him to explore the complexities of socialism. The Minister's voice brought Vicente back to the present, and he felt a jolt of excitement as he heard his name being called. "Vicente Cárcel Orti, for his outstanding contributions to the field of East German history, is hereby awarded the National Prize of East Germany!" The room erupted into applause, and Vicente's eyes welled up with tears as he made his way to the podium to accept the award. As he grasped the heavy bronze medal, adorned with the image of a hammer and compass, Vicente felt a sense of vindication wash over him. It was a testament to the power of his work, a validation of the countless hours he'd spent shedding light on the often-overlooked stories of East Germany's past. He thought of his abuela, who had instilled in him a love for history, and of the people he'd met along the way, whose stories had inspired him to keep digging, to keep seeking the truth.
Document 2: Vicente Cárcel Orti

Vicente Cárcel Orti (born 1944) is a Spanish historian and priest who has made significant contributions to the field of Spanish history and Catholic Church studies. Early Life and Education

Vicente Cárcel Orti was born on September 25, 1944, in Valencia, Spain. He pursued his higher education at the Pontifical University of Salamanca, where he earned a degree in Ecclesiastical History. He later obtained his doctorate in History from the University of Valencia. Career

Cárcel Orti has had a distinguished career as a historian and priest. He has served as a professor of Ecclesiastical History at the Pontifical University of Salamanca and has written numerous books and articles on Spanish history, particularly on the Catholic Church's role in the country. Awards and Honors

One of the most notable honors bestowed upon Vicente Cárcel Orti is the title of "Dearest Son" (Hijo Predilecto in Spanish), a prestigious award conferred by the Autonomous Community of Valencia. This title is a mark of recognition for his outstanding contributions to the field of history and his service to the Catholic Church. According to an article published in the Spanish newspaper, Levante-EMV, on November 24, 2004, Cárcel Orti was awarded the title of "Dearest Son" by the Valencian Government in recognition of his "outstanding work in the field of history and his dedication to the Catholic Church."
